_profile_comment: Workspace profile for the DEFAULT workspace (autopilot/profiles/<profile>.json). Holds this project's backlog seed, task selection filters, goal phases, and implementer prompt rules — extracted out of the generic engine. 'rushpoint' preserves the current behavior; 'generic' (or omitting this) gives a project-neutral engine. A named workspace in workspaces.json sets its own `profile`.
_provider_comment: Active model provider (autopilot/lib/providers/). 'claude' (default) wraps the Anthropic CLI. Routing/budgeting/verification are provider-neutral (they work in LOGICAL tiers strong|mid|cheap + tokens); swapping to another provider = add an adapter under lib/providers/, register it, set this id, and point config.models at that provider's ids. No core-policy change. For per-role provider routing, see the 'providers' block below.
_providers_comment: Provider-mapping system (U-42, autopilot/core/providers.mjs). Defines the base set of model providers and maps agent roles to them. All three types are built-in (claude/openrouter/custom) — omitting this block keeps the engine on the single global config.provider ('claude') with zero behavior change. To route a specific role via OpenRouter, set providers.roleMap.reviewer='openrouter' and add your key via apiKeyEnv. See autopilot/docs/PROVIDER_CONFIG.md for full examples.

definitions.name: anthropic
definitions._note: Anthropic CLI adapter (default). Uses config.cli.bin + config.models for model IDs. No baseURL needed — the CLI handles auth via CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

definitions.name: openrouter
definitions._note: OpenRouter gateway (200+ models). Set OPENROUTER_API_KEY in env. modelId defaults to 'openrouter/auto' (best available) — override with a specific slug like 'anthropic/claude-opus-4'.

definitions.name: custom
definitions._note: Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, Mistral API…). Set baseURL to your server (e.g. http://localhost:11434) and modelId to your model name. apiKeyEnv is optional for auth-free local servers.

roleMap._comment: Map each agent role to a provider name from definitions[].name above. Roles not listed fall back to the global config.provider. Example: set 'reviewer' to 'openrouter' to run code review against a cheaper model while keeping the implementer on Anthropic.

_architect_comment: Stage 2 — Architect Mode (autopilot/lib/architect.mjs + core/architect/). A macro-vision prompt ("Build a real-time chat app from scratch") is NOT routed to the per-cycle implementer; the Architect invokes the PREMIUM tier (Fable 5 — Mythos-class, superior long-context + multi-step planning) to map the architecture and decompose it into a structured backlog of 20–40 granular sub-tasks with dependencies (parent_task_id + deps). models.architect resolves the 'premium' logical tier; architectMinTasks/architectMaxTasks bound the decomposition; autoTrigger gates whether a detected macro-vision inbox task is decomposed automatically.
_api_pools_comment: Stage 1 — API key pooling & load balancing (autopilot/lib/key-manager.mjs). DEPRECATES a single global API key: the engine round-robins a POOL of accounts and rotates off any that hit a 429 or exhaust their daily budget, so one rate-limited account no longer stalls the loop. SECRETS NEVER LIVE HERE — each entry names an env var (`key_env`) read at runtime from process.env. Entry shape: { id, provider: 'anthropic'|'openrouter'|'openai', key_env, status: 'active'|'exhausted'|'rate-limited', daily_budget (USD; 0 = uncapped), current_usage (USD), retry_after (null|ISO date) }. Empty array = single pinned-account mode (current behavior). Rotation engages only when an entry's env token is present. See config.json.example for a populated sample.
_keyRotation_comment: Tuning for the key-rotation wrapper. maxRetries = key rotations per call before surfacing AllKeysExhaustedError (which the supervisor treats as a normal rate-limit cooldown). defaultCooldownMs = fallback cooldown when a 429 carries no retry-after hint. providerMap maps the adapter id (config.provider, e.g. 'claude') to the pool entry `provider` name (e.g. 'anthropic').

implementerRouting._comment: RISK-AWARE routing (2026-06-05): risk>=opusMinRisk OR an architectural opusKeyword -> Opus; everything else (low-risk polish/UI/reliability) -> Sonnet. Replaced the prior all-Opus alwaysOpusGoals policy that caused ~50 rate-limit pauses.

queues._comment: Engine queue/state directory targets (U-31), resolved relative to the autopilot/ dir. inboxDir = where user task files are dropped (the INBOX queue); stateDir = state.json + the backlog/done/blocked markdown mirrors and locks (the BACKLOG/DONE queues live here); handoffDir = the per-role handoff JSON. Defaults match the original hardcoded layout, so leaving these untouched is a no-op. Relocating/onboarding = edit these values only. Consumed via autopilot/config-loader.mjs → { queuePaths }.

paths._comment: Project-agnostic root paths (U-25). appRoot is relative to the autopilot/ parent (the repo root); every other dir is relative to appRoot. Onboarding a new project = edit these values only, no engine code change. Consumed via autopilot/config-loader.mjs → { paths }.

taskClasses._comment: Task taxonomy that drives class-aware selection + review (autopilot/lib/task-class.mjs). Each task is classified product | engine | maintenance | migration by its title prefix ("architecture: …") then goal then this map. WHY: the engine's own source lives in the gitignored /autopilot/ tree, so engine/internal work produces NO git diff and can never pass a product-delivery (player-visible-UI) review gate — that contradiction is the deadlock. Classification lets the reviewer apply the RIGHT gate: product → visible-change gate (unchanged); engine/maintenance/migration → on-disk EVIDENCE gate (artifact exists AND is wired). OPTIONAL OVERRIDES: `map` (goal/prefix → class), `policy` (per-class {productGate, evidence, gitDiffRequired, allowGitignored}), `default` (class for unclassifiable tasks; 'product' keeps the strict gate). Omit this whole block to use the built-in DEFAULTS (which preserve today's product-gate behavior and only relax it for clearly engine/internal work).

budgetGovernor._safeMode_comment: P4 — Usage-limit discovery. detectQuotaMode() classifies the spending ceiling as 'known' (explicit weeklyTokenQuota), 'estimated' (only a per-project maxTokensPerCycle cap), or 'unknown' (neither). With safeMode:true the governor NEVER assumes unlimited: an 'estimated' quota uses the tighter safe* fractions (higher reserve, earlier downgrade/stop), and an 'unknown' quota holds a standing DOWNGRADE posture (cheaper models) — it still never STOPS on an unknown quota, so it cannot deadlock. safeMode:false (default) preserves the prior behavior exactly (unknown quota ⇒ always proceed). quotaMode is persisted to state.budget every cycle.
budgetGovernor._comment: DETERMINISTIC pre-cycle budget gate (autopilot/lib/budget-governor.mjs). Before each cycle a FORMULA (no LLM) decides proceed | downgrade | stop, preventing overspend BEFORE it happens. Q=weeklyTokenQuota (else the per-project cap budgets[project].maxTokensPerCycle, else ∞ → always proceed, backward compatible). S=window tokens spent (state.usage in+out). avg=S/cycles. E=max(minCycleTokens,avg)×(1+safetyMargin)×retryBuffer (conservative, retry-padded). U=Q×(1−reserveFraction) (reserve withheld). P=S+E. Decision: S≥Q×hardStopFraction → STOP (hard quota guard); P>U → STOP (next cycle breaches usable); P>U×downgradeFraction → DOWNGRADE (cheaper models, via lib/route.mjs); else PROCEED. STOP writes the STOP flag (stop early to protect quota; resume after the weekly window resets). Tune thresholds here; enabled:false disables the governor.
budgetGovernor._audit: Every cycle persists the decision to state.budget {action,reason,spent,quota,usable,projected,estimate,cyclesLeft,fractionUsed,at}. Inspect token-free with: node autopilot/supervisor.mjs verify

circuitBreaker._comment: Engine safety halt (SaaS hardening). The supervisor runs unattended against a SHARED paid Claude account, so a runaway state must STOP the loop, not burn the account. Trips (writes the STOP flag → watchdog stays down) when ANY threshold is hit: maxConsecutiveFailures back-to-back crash cycles, maxConsecutiveRateLimits back-to-back rate-limit hits, maxConsecutiveUnproductive back-to-back non-merge cycles (churn), or window spend ≥ maxWindowCostUsd (state.usage.costUsd; null = off). A 'merged' cycle clears the streaks. Set any threshold to 0/null to disable that condition; enabled:false disables the breaker entirely (backward compatible). Resume after fixing the cause: `node autopilot/supervisor.mjs reset-breaker`. Consumed by autopilot/lib/circuit-breaker.mjs + supervisor.mjs.

weeklyBudget._comment: Weekly usage governor (2026-06-05). Account spendora.tracker@gmail.com is SHARED between the kinetic and the user's own Claude sessions, so we pace by cadence (a min gap between cycle starts = 24h/maxCyclesPerDay) to spread consumption evenly to resetAt and leave headroom for the user. The kinetic self-meters its own tokens/cost (state.usage) for visibility; tune maxCyclesPerDay up/down after watching the real burn. Window auto-rolls every resetIntervalDays.

budgets._comment: Per-project token budgets (U-33). Each key is a projectId (the repo+goal slug from lib/lock-manager.mjs resolveRepoGoal — here repo 'Rushpoint-kinetic' + branch suffix 'topo'). maxTokensPerCycle caps that project's cumulative tokens for the current pacing window; maxSpendPerEvent reserves a per-event dollar ceiling for forward use. Counters live in state.tokenSpent[projectId] (lib/token-counter.mjs); the pacer checks them in lib/token-pacer.mjs → isWithinBudget. Two projects each get an independent entry, so one exhausting its budget never throttles another. Omit this whole block to keep cadence-only weekly pacing (backward compatible). Consumed via autopilot/config-loader.mjs → { budgets }.

validation._comment: Project-specific validation commands (U-26). These RushPoint commands (typecheck/build-admin/lint/e2e) live here in config.json, NOT in engine code — onboarding a new project = edit this array only, no supervisor/validate change. A failing `required` command fails the cycle; non-required is a non-blocking warning. The `lint` command also feeds the lint-regression guard. Consumed via autopilot/config-loader.mjs → { validation } and autopilot/lib/validate.mjs.

autoFix._comment: Auto-fix configuration (U-46). Pre-flight linting and import-sorting before AI invocation to eliminate trivial fixable issues. Runs BEFORE validation; if auto-fixes resolve all issues, AI revision is skipped entirely. `enabled:true` activates; `lintFixCommand` and `importSortCommand` define the commands (empty string disables). Execution order: eslint --fix FIRST (via `lintFixCommand`), then prettier for import/format ordering SECOND (via `importSortCommand`). Omit this block or set `enabled:false` to disable (fully backward compatible). Consumed via autopilot/config-loader.mjs → { autoFix } and autopilot/lib/auto-fix.mjs.

telemetry._comment: Decoupled engine telemetry (U-36), resolved by autopilot/config-loader.mjs → { telemetry } and consumed by autopilot/lib/telemetry.mjs. Reports the AUTOPILOT ENGINE's own health/metrics (cycle duration, token count, error count, an event log) INDEPENDENTLY of the RushPoint product — supervisor.mjs + watchdog.mjs emit events at startup / cycle-start / cycle-end / on-error. State persists in state.json under framework.telemetry (separate from the app tier). `enabled:false` makes every recorder a no-op (disable without touching supervisor logic); set `endpoint` to a monitoring URL to batch events out, else they buffer locally. Omit this whole block to default to disabled (backward compatible).

git._comment: Git target (U-35), resolved by autopilot/lib/git-config-loader.mjs → resolveGitConfig(). The engine drives THIS repo/branch. integrationBranch = the branch all reviewed work lands on; baseBranch = where it forks from; commitPrefix = the auto-commit message prefix. THREE OPTIONAL fields make the engine portable to any external repo: `repository` (path to the target repo, relative to the autopilot/ parent or absolute — default '.', the repo the kinetic lives in), `branch` (the active branch — default = integrationBranch), and `worktreeName` (manage the target in a dedicated git worktree placed as a sibling of `repository` — default absent = operate in-place). Omit all three (as here) to keep the current RushPoint in-place layout (fully backward compatible). The watchdog initializes/creates any configured worktree on startup and passes the resolved working-tree root to the supervisor via KINETIC_GIT_ROOT. See autopilot/docs/git-config.md.

_disableDependencyOptimization_comment: U-45 safety valve. Set to true to revert to full-file loading in the Selector (skips the AST-based dep-graph filter). Useful for debugging or comparing token counts. False (default) = optimization active when a contextProvider is enabled.
_profileSelectorTokens_comment: U-45 measurement flag. Set to true to log before/after file counts for every Selector context-map filter pass (stdout, [dep-opt] prefix). Enables benchmarking the token-reduction claim on a representative 5-file feature.

contextProvider._comment: External codebase-context seam (U-37), resolved by autopilot/config-loader.mjs → { contextProvider } and consumed by autopilot/core/context-provider.mjs + core/selector. A host app can pre-compute its own codebase maps (FileIndexMap/SymbolIndexMap/DependencyGraph) and feed them to the selector so it skips redundant local file scanning. REQUIRED fields: `interface` (the contract a provider implements — the module#export the host targets), `source` (an id for the provider/codebase, also the cache key), `cacheStrategy` ('memory' = reuse a loaded bundle while fresh; 'none' = always re-resolve). OPTIONAL fallback fields: `validateFreshness` (reject maps older than maxStaleMs and fall back to local analysis), `maxStaleMs` (freshness window, default 300000 = 5 min), `fallbackToLocal` (silently use local file-system analysis when no/stale/invalid maps — default true; keeps standalone mode working). `enabled:false` (the default) keeps the engine on pure local analysis — fully backward compatible. See autopilot/docs/context-provider.md.

handoff._comment: Per-role handoff file context tag (U-34), resolved by autopilot/lib/handoff-paths.mjs. `context` is inserted before the extension of every handoff basename (selection.json -> selection-rushpoint-kinetic-topo.json; same for implementation/review/audit) so two project contexts that share a handoff dir never overwrite each other. Omit `context` to derive it from the repo+goal slug (the same identity used by locks/budgets); omit the whole block (and have no derivable repo/goal) to keep the legacy generic 'selection.json' basenames (backward compatible). See autopilot/HANDOFF_STRUCTURE.md.

locks._comment: Process-lock filenames (U-32), resolved at engine startup by autopilot/lib/lock-manager.mjs. {repoGoal} expands to the active target repo + goal segment (repo dir name + the git.integrationBranch suffix after '/', e.g. 'rushpoint-kinetic-topo') so two kinetic instances against different targets/goals never share a lock. Optionally set locks.repoGoal to override the derived segment. Omit this whole `locks` block for the legacy hardcoded 'watchdog.lock'/'supervisor.lock' basenames (backward compatible — graceful fallback, no breaking change). Consumed via autopilot/lib/lock-manager.mjs → { lockPaths }.
